Summary  
Data source overview: The 8-page extract is MIRI’s “2015 in review” report.  It surveys the institute’s research on agent-foundations safety problems (logical uncertainty, corrigibility, mild optimisation, etc.) and highlights three concrete technical strands: Reflective Oracles, Safely-Interruptible Agents, and Quantilizers.  Each strand supplies a complete reasoning chain from an identified failure mode to a theoretically grounded mitigation.

Inference strategy justification:  The document is a narrative progress report, not a formal paper, so the causal chains are dispersed across many paragraphs.  I distilled the three strands that are explicitly presented as new results and safety approaches, then reconstructed their risk-to-intervention logic using MIRI’s own headings (e.g. “Safely Interruptible Agents”, “Quantilizers: A Safer Alternative …”, “Reflective Oracles”).  Only modest inference (confidence level 2) was required to place each idea in the six requested concept categories and to infer practical intervention phrasing.

Extraction completeness explanation:  All claims that form essential parts of the three presented mitigation pathways were captured.  Each node appears in at least one edge, and the three pathways share the same top-level risk node, forming one connected knowledge fabric with no satellites.

Key limitations:  
• The source material is wide-ranging; minor research threads (e.g. Vingean reflection, value specification case studies) were excluded to keep the fabric coherent.  
• Validation evidence is theoretical rather than empirical, so edge confidence rarely exceeds 4.  
• Lifecycle and maturity values for interventions are estimated from publication context; no deployment data are available.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[78] – High confidence that all mandatory criteria are met and JSON is syntactically valid, but moderate uncertainty remains in mapping broad narrative text onto precise node categories.

Instruction-set improvement suggestion:  Provide an explicit allowance for grouping several closely-related research outputs under one combined “validation evidence” node to avoid unnecessary proliferation when multiple proofs support the same design.
